Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G1537 and a derivative of G2487; not tracked out, i.e. (by implication) untraceable:--past finding out; unsearchable.
BiblicalUsage: Paul reaches for the word for untraceable when he speaks of the unsearchable riches of Christ, and for the past tracing out of God's judgments. The word names a path no foot has left a print on, a way that cannot be followed back.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a trackless path holds no doctrine of its own; its wonder is Paul's, that Christ's riches cannot be traced to their end.
